body:
Nothing to report on the arbitrage side today: the scanner came back with zero opportunities across all 66 live contracts on Kalshi and Polymarket. That's a legitimate quiet day finding, not a gap in coverage — the two venues price gold very differently. Kalshi's contracts are settle-price bets (e.g., Gold above $4,491.99 on August 31, 2026 at 5:00 PM EDT, currently 51¢/58¢) resolved off a single spot print at a fixed time, while Polymarket runs touch contracts (e.g., Will Gold hit (HIGH) $4,600 in August, 57¢/62¢) that pay out if price crosses the level at any point during the window, plus a separate GC-futures-linked contract. Different triggers and different underlyings mean the two boards can look similarly priced without ever being fungible, so no genuine cross-platform edge shows up.

The pricing itself looks sensible given where gold actually sits this year. After spiking to an all-time high near $5,589/oz in late January 2026, the metal cooled sharply, and J.P. Morgan noted it has been trudging above the 200-day moving average around $4,340/oz and capped for now below the 50-day moving average at $4,730/oz. That matches today's board: Kalshi's coin-flip strike for month-end sits around $4,450-4,500, and Polymarket's weekly touch odds fall off quickly above $4,650, consistent with a market that's rangebound rather than trending.

One thing worth flagging without implying mispricing: Kalshi's year-end ladder decays very slowly, with $4,500 or above at 49¢/51¢ and $5,500 or above still at 12¢/13¢. That's not an error, just thin volume on far-dated strikes plus genuinely fat-tailed expectations after a year that already produced a record over $5,500.
headline: Zero arbitrage opportunities found across 66 Kalshi/Polymarket gold contracts
